summary: Yinggang Sun is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Sun held a post at Fudan University (attested 2014) and served as a research fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yingshan Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen was a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996) and became an honorary research fellow there, retiring in February 2023.
Yingxue Wang works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Wang completed a BA at Yale University (2013-2017) and an MA at Harvard University (2017-2025).

Yinke Chen (1890-1969) was a Sinologist, historian, and linguist. He studied at Kobun Gakuin, Fudan, Berlin, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard under Lanman, Lüders, Müller, and Haenisch, and later taught at Tsinghua, Peking University, and Sun Yat-sen University.

Yinshun (1906-2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Qingnian and Taixu, earning a doctorate from Taisho University. He taught at the Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes and served as president of the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

Yirmiyahu Yovel (1935-2018) was a philosopher. He was educated at the Hebrew Reali School and later completed his studies at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (c. 1957-1968) and Princeton University (c. 1966-1968).
Yiu Wing Chan specializes in Buddhist studies. Chan earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong by 2013, studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann (1937-2023) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv University, Hanazono University, and Kyoto University (PhD) under Sojo Hirano and Ben-Ami Scharfstein, and became a professor at the University of Haifa.

Yogendra Bhardwaj works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University (2018-2021) and was appointed assistant professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in 2025.
Yohei Furukawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Takatsugu Hayashi. He is attested as an associate professor at Soka University in 2026.

Yohei Kawajiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. Kawajiri served as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008-2013, 2022) and was a JSPS special research fellow (attested 2011).

Yoichi Fukuda (born 1954) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986-1991) and later served as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003, 2015).
Yoichi Kawada (born 1937) is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He served as the director of the Institute of Oriental Philosophy (attested in 2002 and 2016).
Yong Hua specializes in Buddhist studies. Hua earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014), where the program was supervised by Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.

Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak (born 1926) specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tingchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri Monastery under Gangru Tsultrim Gyaltsen and Sangye Tenzin, later serving as lopön at Menri and Triten Norbutse.

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche (born 1975) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sherab Ling Monastery and Dzongsar Institute under Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Khenpo Kunga Wangchuk, later serving as abbot of Sherab Ling.
Yongshan He specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, as well as under Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang (1893-1964) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Tsinghua and Harvard under Lanman and Babbitt, he was a professor at Southeast, National Central, and Peking universities, also serving as Peking University's vice president.

Yongyu Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a BA from Cornell University and was a PhD student at Harvard University. Chen served as a professor at Joong-Ang Sangha University (attested 2015) and an ArtTable Fellow at Public Art Fund (2025).

Yonten Gyatso (1933-2002) was a Tibetologist and historian. He earned a Geshé degree from Drepung Gomang Dratsang and a diploma from the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he later served as a research advisor in Tibetan Studies.
